page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is provisioned through a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor providing 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, complete with 35 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction support. System memory totals 64.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Acceleration is handled by a single discrete NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM. Ephemeral storage is provided by a 225 GB local NVMe SSD, and the platform delivers a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance tiers across subsystems. Single-core processing registers in the lower quartile, characterized by a stress-ng single-core score of 1286.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1144.0. Multi-core performance operates within the median spectrum, achieving 13549.68 in stress-ng and 7019.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing. Memory throughput benchmarks similarly align with median averages, posting 88.11 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 45.9 GB/sec for large-block writes. Static web throughput and Redis operations also demonstrate middle-tier capacity at 11.51 GB/sec and 13.26 million operations per second respectively.

GPU-driven workloads represent the primary strength of this configuration. In language model evaluation, the NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers top-tier prompt processing throughput, reaching 8447.43 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 1163.92 tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Text generation maintains strong upper-quartile marks, yielding 321.44 tokens per second on the 135M architecture and 40.25 tokens per second on 7B models. Throughput degrades substantially when moving to 70B parameter models, where prompt processing falls to 13.51 tokens per second due to the constraint of 16 GB total GPU memory.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance balances specialized tensor acceleration with moderate host CPU capacity, avoiding the higher resource commitments of enterprise training instances. This architectural combination makes it appropriate for production machine learning inference on small to mid-sized models, video transcoding pipelines, 3D graphics rendering, and inference-driven microservices requiring dedicated local NVMe caching.

A single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM provides dedicated acceleration.
